question: What is the divine source, purpose, and angelic delivery of the final canonical book of the New Testament?
opt1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass; and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John
opt2: The personal memoirs of John composed in Ephesus, which the elders preserved for future generations
opt3: The prophetic discourse of Paul received in Rome, which Luke recorded and delivered to the churches
opt4: The secret apocalyptic apocalypse discovered in the caves of Patmos by Jewish pilgrims
correct: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass; and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John
explanation: The book opens by declaring its transcendent origin from God the Father through Jesus Christ, communicated via His angel to John. Revelation 1:1 (KJV) - "The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass; and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John:"

question: What unique beatitude is pronounced in Revelation 1:3 upon those who engage with this prophetic revelation?
opt1: Blessed are they that calculate the exact calendar day of Christ's return before all nations
opt2: Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand
opt3: Blessed are they that keep the ceremonial ordinances and sabbaths of the Mosaic covenant
opt4: Blessed are they that build monumental basilicas in the seven cities of the Roman province of Asia
correct: Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand
explanation: A special blessing is pronounced upon both the public reader and attentive hearers who treasure and obey this prophecy, because the time of fulfillment is near. Revelation 1:3 (KJV) - "Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand."

question: How does John ascribe praise to Jesus Christ in his opening doxology regarding redemption and royal status?
opt1: Unto Him that taught us philosophical ethics, and made us municipal judges in Roman courts
opt2: Unto Him that restored the earthly kingdom of David, and crowned us as temporal rulers in Jerusalem
opt3: Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, and hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father
opt4: Unto Him that preserved our mortal bodies from sickness, and granted us material wealth on earth
correct: Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, and hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father
explanation: Christ's supreme redemptive work is celebrated: He loved us, cleansed us from sin through His atoning blood, and elevated believers into a kingdom of royal priests. Revelation 1:5-6 (KJV) - "Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen."

question: What universal, visible manifestation will accompany the glorious advent of Jesus Christ according to Revelation 1:7?
opt1: Behold, He cometh secretly into subterranean caverns, known only to initiates of ancient mysteries
opt2: Behold, He cometh riding an earthly chariot into the Sanhedrin court to restore the temple sacrifices
opt3: Behold, He cometh as a philosophical teacher to the academic forums of Athens and Alexandria
opt4: Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him
correct: Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him
explanation: The Second Coming will be universally visible, witnessed by every human eye, including those responsible for His crucifixion, causing all tribes of the earth to mourn. Revelation 1:7 (KJV) - "Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen."

question: What majestic divine title does the Lord God proclaim concerning His eternal sovereignty in Revelation 1:8?
opt1: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty
opt2: I am the guardian angel of the province of Asia, who watches over the seven cities of the empire
opt3: I am the spirit of prophecy that inspires mortal sages to write moral laws for humanity
opt4: I am the prince of the kings of the earth who reigns from an earthly palace in Jerusalem
correct: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty
explanation: The Lord God asserts His timeless eternity and omnipotence using the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, affirming He is, was, and is to come. Revelation 1:8 (KJV) - "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty."

question: Where was John when he received this apocalyptic revelation, on what day, and in what spiritual state?
opt1: In the city of Antioch, in fasting and prayer during the feast of tabernacles
opt2: In the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ; in the Spirit on the Lord's day
opt3: In the temple of Jerusalem, praying at the ninth hour of the evening sacrifice
opt4: In the catacombs of Rome, awaiting execution under imperial decree on the sabbath
correct: In the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ; in the Spirit on the Lord's day
explanation: Exiled to the Aegean island of Patmos for his fidelity to God's Word, John was filled with the Holy Spirit on Sunday, the Lord's Day, when he heard a trumpet-like voice. Revelation 1:9-10 (KJV) - "I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ. I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day, and heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet,"

question: How does John describe the appearance of the Son of Man standing in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks?
opt1: Wearing the ragged tunic of a Galilean carpenter, holding a wooden shepherd's staff and a horn of oil
opt2: Dressed in purple imperial robes, wearing a crown of jewels and bearing the golden scepter of Caesar
opt3: Clothed with a garment down to the foot, girt about the paps with a golden girdle; his head and hairs white like wool, his eyes as a flame of fire, and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword
opt4: Adorned as a high priest with the breastplate of twelve stones, blowing a silver trumpet of jubilee
correct: Clothed with a garment down to the foot, girt about the paps with a golden girdle; his head and hairs white like wool, his eyes as a flame of fire, and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword
explanation: John beholds the glorified Christ as supreme Judge and Priest, characterized by divine wisdom, piercing holy gaze, blazing feet, and the sharp twoedged sword of His Word. Revelation 1:13-16 (KJV) - "And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle. His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters. And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength."

question: When John fell at His feet as dead, what comforting declaration and sovereign authority did Christ pronounce?
opt1: Stand up, for I am thy fellowservant and an angel sent from the celestial throne of glory
opt2: Weep not, for the kingdom of Rome will crumble before the end of this present generation
opt3: Arise, and build seven stone altars in the wilderness of Patmos to offer morning sacrifices
opt4: Fear not; I am the first and the last: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death
correct: Fear not; I am the first and the last: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death
explanation: The living Christ reassures John of His eternal victory over mortality, declaring that He possesses supreme authority over death and the realm of the dead (Hades). Revelation 1:17-18 (KJV) - "And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead. And he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death."

question: What threefold chronological outline was John commanded to write down in Revelation 1:19?
opt1: Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter
opt2: Write the history of the patriarchs, the laws of the tabernacle, and the deeds of the kings of Judah
opt3: Write the genealogy of the apostles, the minutes of the council of Jerusalem, and the epistles of Paul
opt4: Write the grievances of the poor, the taxation codes of Asia, and the civil decrees of the governors
correct: Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter
explanation: This key verse provides the divinely inspired structural framework of the Apocalypse: past vision (chapter 1), present church age (chapters 2-3), and future eschatological events (chapters 4-22). Revelation 1:19 (KJV) - "Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter;"

question: What is the divine mystery and interpretation of the seven stars and the seven golden candlesticks seen by John?
opt1: The seven stars are the seven archangels of heaven, and the candlesticks are the seven sacraments of the church
opt2: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches
opt3: The seven stars are the planets of the solar system, and the candlesticks are the days of the creation week
opt4: The seven stars are the principalities of Roman provinces, and the candlesticks are the hills of the city of Rome
correct: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches
explanation: Christ Himself interprets the symbols: the seven stars represent the messengers/leaders of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands represent the local assemblies illuminating the world. Revelation 1:20 (KJV) - "The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches."

question: What serious spiritual defect did Christ charge against the otherwise diligent and doctrinally discerning church at Ephesus?
opt1: Thou hast openly tolerated the idolatrous sacrifices offered at the temple of Diana
opt2: Thou hast denied the resurrection of the dead and embraced pagan philosophy
opt3: Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love
opt4: Thou hast refused to practice manual labor and become dependent on municipal welfare
correct: Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love
explanation: Despite their tireless labor and intolerance of false apostles, the Ephesian church had abandoned the fervent, devoted love that originally characterized their devotion to Christ. Revelation 2:4 (KJV) - "Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love."

question: What promise is granted to the overcomer in the letter to the church at Ephesus?
opt1: He shall sit upon the golden throne of Solomon and rule the twelve tribes of Israel
opt2: He shall receive an earthly crown of laurels and municipal citizenship in Ephesus
opt3: He shall be exempt from all physical sickness and live for one thousand years on earth
opt4: To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God
correct: To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God
explanation: Overcoming Ephesians are promised access to the Tree of Life in God's celestial paradise, reversing the Edenic curse and granting eternal communion with God. Revelation 2:7 (KJV) - "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God."

question: What impending trial and reward did Christ announce to the suffering and impoverished church at Smyrna?
opt1: Ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life
opt2: Ye shall be delivered from all imprisonment and receive great financial wealth from Roman magistrates
opt3: Ye shall escape to the wilderness of Cappadocia and build a secure underground sanctuary
opt4: Ye shall conquer your persecutors by military force and establish an earthly Christian empire
correct: Ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life
explanation: Smyrna received no rebuke, only encouragement to remain steadfast through ten days of testing, even unto martyrdom, with the pledge of the crown of life. Revelation 2:10 (KJV) - "Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life."

question: What divine promise protects the faithful overcomer in the church at Smyrna from ultimate eternal harm?
opt1: He that overcometh shall never experience physical illness or bodily pain on earth
opt2: He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death
opt3: He that overcometh shall inherit vast vineyards and estates throughout Asia Minor
opt4: He that overcometh shall possess miraculous authority to command angelic legions
correct: He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death
explanation: The believer who conquers through faith is guaranteed absolute immunity from the 'second death'--the lake of fire and final judgment. Revelation 2:11 (KJV) - "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death."

question: Where did the church at Pergamos dwell, and what corrupt doctrine did they tolerate in their midst?
opt1: Where the Roman Senate convenes: holding the philosophy of the Stoics who deny the resurrection
opt2: Where the temple of Diana stands: holding the rites of the magicians who trade in secret incantations
opt3: Where Satan's seat is: holding the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, and the doctrine of the Nicolaitanes
opt4: Where the school of Alexandria flourishes: holding the allegorical methods of Greek scholars
correct: Where Satan's seat is: holding the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, and the doctrine of the Nicolaitanes
explanation: Pergamos, center of imperial cult worship ('Satan's seat'), was rebuked for tolerating antinomian compromises: the doctrine of Balaam (idolatry and sexual immorality) and the Nicolaitanes. Revelation 2:14-15 (KJV) - "But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication. So hast thou also them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitanes, which thing I hate."

question: What two mysterious heavenly rewards are promised to the overcomer in the letter to Pergamos?
opt1: To sit on the judgment seat of Caesar, and wear an imperial purple robe embroidered with gold
opt2: To possess the golden key of David, and command the angels that guard the Euphrates river
opt3: To drink of the river of milk and honey, and receive a golden harp inscribed with ancient psalms
opt4: To eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it
correct: To eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it
explanation: Christ promises the overcomer spiritual sustenance (hidden manna) and an intimate token of acquittal and special favor (a white stone with an inscribed new name). Revelation 2:17 (KJV) - "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it."

question: What false prophetess did the church at Thyatira tolerate, and what corrupt practices did she teach God's servants?
opt1: That woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols
opt2: The sorceress Athaliah, who compelled the elders to worship the golden calves of Samaria
opt3: The diviner of Endor, who practiced necromancy and invoked ancestral spirits in the assembly
opt4: The daughter of Herodias, who seduced the youth through theatrical dances and pagan feasts
correct: That woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols
explanation: Thyatira was severely rebuked for tolerating a self-styled prophetess symbolically named Jezebel, who led believers into pagan idolatry and sexual immorality. Revelation 2:20 (KJV) - "Notwithstanding I have a few things against thee, because thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols."

question: What profound omniscience does the Son of God claim when warning the church at Thyatira concerning His judgment?
opt1: And all the nations shall know that I measure the wealth and military armaments of earthly kingdoms
opt2: And all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works
opt3: And all the governors shall know that I examine municipal legal statutes to determine civic penalties
opt4: And all the assemblies shall know that I count the monetary tithes deposited in temple chests
correct: And all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works
explanation: Christ claims the divine prerogative of searching the deepest inner motives and thoughts ('reins and hearts'), executing impartial and righteous recompense upon every individual. Revelation 2:23 (KJV) - "And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works."

question: What authority over nations is granted to the faithful overcomer who keeps Christ's works unto the end in Thyatira?
opt1: He shall receive diplomatic immunity from all pagan courts and govern Roman trade routes
opt2: He shall negotiate peace treaties among the barbarian kings of the northern wilderness
opt3: To him will I give power over the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers
opt4: He shall rebuild the ancient walls of Jerusalem and command an earthly cavalry of horses
correct: To him will I give power over the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers
explanation: The overcomer is promised a share in Christ's messianic millennial reign (citing Psalm 2), ruling the nations with righteous firmness depicted as a rod of iron. Revelation 2:26-27 (KJV) - "And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father."

question: What celestial gift does Christ promise to bestow upon the overcomer in Thyatira alongside authority over nations?
opt1: And I will give him the golden chariot of Elijah
opt2: And I will give him the horn of anointing from the tabernacle
opt3: And I will give him the emerald crown of the archangels
opt4: And I will give him the morning star
correct: And I will give him the morning star
explanation: Christ promises to give the overcomer the 'morning star'--which is Christ Himself in His glorious resurrection presence (Revelation 22:16) and herald of the eternal day. Revelation 2:28 (KJV) - "And I will give him the morning star."

question: What devastating diagnosis does Christ pronounce against the church in Sardis despite its outward reputation?
opt1: I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead
opt2: Thou hast been completely destroyed by the persecution of Roman soldiers
opt3: Thou hast lost all financial resources and can no longer care for widows
opt4: Thou hast compromised with Greek philosophy and rejected the doctrine of creation
correct: I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead
explanation: Sardis enjoyed a glittering reputation among men for vitality, yet in the penetrating assessment of Christ, the assembly was spiritually lifeless and dead. Revelation 3:1 (KJV) - "And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars; I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead."

question: What commendation and heavenly promises are given to the undefiled remnant in Sardis who overcome?
opt1: They shall receive golden laurels from the Roman senate, and their deeds shall be carved on municipal arches
opt2: They shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life
opt3: They shall be appointed governors over the cities of Phrygia, and wear robes of imperial purple
opt4: They shall be exempted from physical mortality, and dwell permanently in earthly palaces of marble
correct: They shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life
explanation: The faithful few who kept their garments undefiled are promised fellowship with Christ in white, enduring clothing of righteousness, and permanent preservation in the Book of Life. Revelation 3:4-5 (KJV) - "Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels."

question: How does Christ reveal Himself to the church in Philadelphia regarding royal authority and access?
opt1: He that hath the signet ring of Solomon, who buildeth the physical sanctuary in Jerusalem
opt2: He that commands the Roman legions, who overthroweth the thrones of pagan governors
opt3: He that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth
opt4: He that holdeth the golden scales of commerce, who multiplieth the trade of Mediterranean harbors
correct: He that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth
explanation: Christ presents Himself as the sovereign possessor of the Key of David, having absolute messianic authority to open doors of gospel opportunity and kingdom access that no human can close. Revelation 3:7 (KJV) - "And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;"

question: Because the church in Philadelphia kept the word of Christ's patience, what deliverance does He promise them?
opt1: I will grant thee immense commercial wealth so that no member experiences poverty
opt2: I will build an impenetrable stone fortress around the city to repel Roman soldiers
opt3: I will ensure that none of thy citizens ever suffer physical bereavement or bereavement
opt4: I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth
correct: I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth
explanation: Because of their steadfast fidelity despite having 'little strength', Christ promises to protect and keep them from the catastrophic global trial destined to test the earth's inhabitants. Revelation 3:10 (KJV) - "Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth."

question: What permanent spiritual pillar and threefold inscription are promised to the overcomer in Philadelphia?
opt1: Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, and my new name
opt2: Him that overcometh will I make an archon in the city council, and write upon him the title of Roman citizen
opt3: Him that overcometh will I make a guardian angel of the Euphrates, and write upon him the seven seals of prophecy
opt4: Him that overcometh will I make a high priest in the temple of Herod, and write upon him the names of the twelve tribes
correct: Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, and my new name
explanation: In a city frequently shattered by earthquakes, Christ promises unshakeable eternal stability: becoming a permanent pillar in God's temple, inscribed with God's name, the New Jerusalem, and Christ's new name. Revelation 3:12 (KJV) - "Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name."

question: How does Christ identify Himself in the opening of His letter to the self-sufficient church of the Laodiceans?
opt1: The prince of Mediterranean merchants, the distributor of civic wealth, the master of gold
opt2: The Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God
opt3: The restorer of the Mosaic tabernacle, the builder of altars, the instructor of scribes
opt4: The archangel of celestial hosts, the commander of legions, the ruler of stars
correct: The Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God
explanation: Christ introduces Himself as the Amen (the final verity), the infallible Witness, and the sovereign Source and Ruler ('beginning') of all God's creation. Revelation 3:14 (KJV) - "And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write; These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God;"

question: What nauseating spiritual temperature did Laodicea exhibit, and what severe reaction did Christ threaten?
opt1: Because thou art freezing in faith, I will cast thee into the scorching sands of the desert
opt2: Because thou art burning with fiery zeal, I will immerse thee in the icy waters of the sea
opt3: I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth
opt4: Because thou art fluctuating like sea waves, I will blow thee away with the east wind
correct: I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth
explanation: Mirroring the tepid, emetic mineral water piped into their city from Hierapolis, Laodicea's sickening spiritual apathy and complacency provoked Christ's disgust. Revelation 3:15-16 (KJV) - "I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth."

question: What stark contrast existed between Laodicea's self-evaluation and Christ's true assessment of their condition?
opt1: Because thou sayest, We are persecuted and weak; and knowest not that thou art politically dominant over Roman governors
opt2: Because thou sayest, We are unlearned in philosophy; and knowest not that thou hast surpassed the scholars of Athens
opt3: Because thou sayest, We are dying of disease; and knowest not that thy bodies are immortal like angels
opt4: Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked
correct: Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked
explanation: Blinded by banking wealth, famous black wool, and eye-salve manufacture, Laodicea thought itself wealthy, while spiritually Christ found them wretched, bankrupt, blind, and naked. Revelation 3:17 (KJV) - "Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked:"

question: What divine remedy does Christ counsel the church of Laodicea to purchase from Him?
opt1: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see
opt2: Buy of Me silver from the mines of Spain, and purple dyed garments from the merchants of Tyre
opt3: Buy of Me olive oil from the groves of Galilee, and cedar beams from the forests of Lebanon
opt4: Buy of Me parchment scrolls from Egypt, and bronze shields forged by Roman armorers
correct: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see
explanation: Christ urges them to acquire true spiritual wealth: purified faith (gold tried in fire), imputed righteousness (white raiment), and spiritual illumination (divine eye-salve). Revelation 3:18 (KJV) - "I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see."

question: What gracious invitation and reward does Christ extend to the individual who hears His voice and opens the door in Laodicea?
opt1: Behold, I break open the gates of the city: and all who submit shall receive bags of Roman silver and civic laurels
opt2: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me. To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne
opt3: Behold, I dispatch Michael with a flaming sword: and all who repent shall build a temple on Mount Gerizim
opt4: Behold, I seal the doors of the assembly: and all who remain outside shall be exiled to the mountains of Media
correct: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me. To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne
explanation: Even to a lukewarm church, Christ offers intimate personal fellowship to anyone opening the door, culminating in the astonishing promise of co-reigning on His throne. Revelation 3:20-21 (KJV) - "Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me. To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne."

question: What vision greets John when a door was opened in heaven, and what voice summoned him upward?
opt1: A voice of many waters crying, Flee into the wilderness, for the wrath of God is poured upon the earth
opt2: A sound of thunder announcing, Bow down before the altar of incense, for the high priest is entering
opt3: The first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter
opt4: A choir of angels singing, Peace be upon Jerusalem, for the Roman legions have laid down their swords
correct: The first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter
explanation: John is transported in the Spirit through an open door in heaven, summoned by the trumpet-like voice of Christ to behold future prophetic events. Revelation 4:1 (KJV) - "After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter."

question: How does John describe the glorious appearance of Him who sat upon the heavenly throne and the canopy surrounding it?
opt1: He that sat was like an emperor in robes of purple, crowned with diamonds and holding a silver scepter
opt2: He that sat was like a fiery colossus of bronze, surrounded by clouds of thick black smoke and lightning
opt3: He that sat was like an ancient patriarch with flowing hair, seated beneath a cedar canopy of Lebanon
opt4: And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald
correct: And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald
explanation: God's transcendent majesty is depicted through brilliant gems--dazzling jasper and ruby sardine--encircled by an emerald rainbow testifying to His enduring covenant mercy. Revelation 4:3 (KJV) - "And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald."

question: Who sat upon the four and twenty seats round about the throne, and how were they adorned?
opt1: Four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold
opt2: Four and twenty archangels standing, holding flaming swords and trumpets of brass
opt3: Four and twenty kings of the Gentiles, wearing armor of iron and carrying shields of bronze
opt4: Four and twenty prophets of the Old Testament, bearing wooden yokes and scrolls of lamentations
correct: Four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold
explanation: The twenty-four elders represent the redeemed people of God (Israel's 12 tribes and the 12 apostles), enthroned in priestly white garments and crowned with victor's crowns. Revelation 4:4 (KJV) - "And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold."

question: What emanated from the heavenly throne, and what two features stood immediately before it?
opt1: Out of the throne proceeded torrents of water and hail; and twelve golden altars offering burning incense
opt2: Out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and seven lamps of fire burning, which are the seven Spirits of God; and a sea of glass like unto crystal
opt3: Out of the throne proceeded heavy clouds of darkness; and an iron furnace consuming sacrificial offerings
opt4: Out of the throne proceeded angelic trumpets; and a river of blood flowing toward the gates of the temple
correct: Out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and seven lamps of fire burning, which are the seven Spirits of God; and a sea of glass like unto crystal
explanation: The throne emits manifestations of divine power and majesty, flanked by the seven burning lamps of the Holy Spirit and a serene expanse resembling a crystal sea of glass. Revelation 4:5-6 (KJV) - "And out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and there were seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal:"

question: How does John describe the four living creatures (beasts) in the midst and round about the throne?
opt1: The first was like an ox, the second like a serpent, the third like a horse, and the fourth like a wolf
opt2: The first was like a leopard, the second like a bear, the third like a dragon, and the fourth like a ram
opt3: The first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle
opt4: The first was like a cherub, the second like an elephant, the third like a hawk, and the fourth like a camel
correct: The first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle
explanation: The four cherubic living beings represent the pinnacle of God's creation: wild beasts (lion), domestic animals (calf/ox), humanity (man), and birds (eagle). Revelation 4:7 (KJV) - "And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle."

question: What ceaseless trisagion do the four living creatures proclaim day and night before the throne?
opt1: Mighty, mighty, mighty, Creator of worlds, who ruleth the stars and the planets of heaven
opt2: Righteous, righteous, righteous, Judge of all flesh, who overturneth the kingdoms of men
opt3: Glorious, glorious, glorious, King of Israel, who delivereth the captives from their chains
opt4: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come
correct: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come
explanation: Endowed with six wings and full of eyes, the living creatures offer perpetual adoration to the thrice-holy, eternal, and omnipotent Lord God Almighty. Revelation 4:8 (KJV) - "And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, LORD God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come."

question: What worshipful act do the four and twenty elders perform when the living creatures give glory to Him on the throne?
opt1: Fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that liveth for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne
opt2: Stand in ranks and draw golden swords, swearing an oath of allegiance before the heavenly host
opt3: Play upon silver harps and march in solemn procession around the crystal sea of glass
opt4: Blow twenty-four golden trumpets to summon the angelic armies from the four corners of heaven
correct: Fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that liveth for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne
explanation: In ultimate humility and self-surrender, the elders prostrate themselves before the eternal Sovereign, casting their rewarded crowns at His feet. Revelation 4:10 (KJV) - "The four and twenty elders fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that liveth for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying,"

question: What universal theological reason do the elders proclaim in Revelation 4:11 for God's worthiness to receive all glory, honor, and power?
opt1: Thou art worthy, O Lord: for Thou hast crushed the armies of Pharaoh and drowned the chariots in the sea
opt2: Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created
opt3: Thou art worthy, O Lord: for Thou hast built the earthly city of David with gates of brass and walls of gold
opt4: Thou art worthy, O Lord: for Thou hast granted eternal dominion to the kings of the Gentiles
correct: Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created
explanation: God's worthiness is grounded in His sovereign act of creation: everything in the universe exists solely through His divine will and for His good pleasure. Revelation 4:11 (KJV) - "Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created."

question: Where was the heavenly throne situated in John's vision, and how was the crystal sea positioned?
opt1: The throne was erected upon Mount Zion in Judea, and before it stood the bronze laver of Solomon
opt2: The throne was suspended in the clouds above Rome, and beneath it marched the legions of angels
opt3: Immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne; and before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal
opt4: The throne was hidden inside a cave in Patmos, and before it burned an altar of cedar incense
correct: Immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne; and before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal
explanation: John's spiritual ascension transports him directly before the central throne of heaven, fronted by the pristine, motionless sea of glass reflecting divine holiness. Revelation 4:6 (KJV) - "And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind."

question: How many wings did each of the four living creatures possess, and with what were they filled within and without?
opt1: Each of them had four wings, and they were covered with scales of bronze and silver
opt2: Each of them had two wings, and they were adorned with crowns of emerald and gold
opt3: Each of them had eight wings, and they were holding bowls of incense and olive oil
opt4: And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within
correct: And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within
explanation: Echoing Isaiah's seraphim and Ezekiel's cherubim, each living creature possesses six wings and is filled with eyes, signifying ceaseless vigilance and comprehensive spiritual perception. Revelation 4:8 (KJV) - "And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, LORD God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come."

question: What object did John see in the right hand of Him who sat upon the throne in Revelation 5:1?
opt1: A book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals
opt2: A golden scepter of iron tipped with an emerald, inscribed with the ten commandments
opt3: A silver chalice overflowing with the wine of divine wrath, sealed with the signet of Caesar
opt4: A bronze key engraved with the name of David, wrapped in seven cords of purple linen
correct: A book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals
explanation: The Father holds the title deed of creation and redemption--a scroll completely filled with writing on both sides, legally secured with seven divine seals. Revelation 5:1 (KJV) - "And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals."

question: What challenge did a strong angel proclaim with a loud voice, and what initial crisis caused John to weep much?
opt1: Who can rebuild the temple of Jerusalem? And no architect was found among the nations of the earth
opt2: Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof? And no man in heaven, nor in earth, neither under the earth, was able to open the book, neither to look thereon
opt3: Who can number the stars of the sky? And no astronomer was able to calculate their orbits
opt4: Who can defeat the armies of the dragon? And no general was found capable of bearing the sword
correct: Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof? And no man in heaven, nor in earth, neither under the earth, was able to open the book, neither to look thereon
explanation: The cosmic search found no created being in heaven, earth, or the underworld worthy to break the seals, plunging John into profound grief over the prospect of God's redemptive purpose stalling. Revelation 5:2-4 (KJV) - "And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice, Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof? And no man in heaven, nor in earth, neither under the earth, was able to open the book, neither to look thereon. And I wept much, because no man was found worthy to open and to read the book, neither to look thereon."

question: How did one of the elders comfort weeping John concerning who has prevailed to open the seven-sealed book?
opt1: Weep not: behold, Michael the archangel hath summoned ten thousand seraphim to break the seals
opt2: Weep not: behold, the patriarch Abraham hath offered his merits to unlock the secret scroll
opt3: Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof
opt4: Weep not: behold, the church of the martyrs hath accumulated sufficient prayers to open the book
correct: Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof
explanation: An elder directs John's gaze to the triumphant Messiah, identified by His royal Old Testament titles: the conquering Lion of Judah and the promised Root of David. Revelation 5:5 (KJV) - "And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof."

question: When John turned to see the Lion, what startling figure did he actually behold standing in the midst of the throne?
opt1: A crowned warrior prince astride a white horse, bearing a sharp twoedged broadsword
opt2: A celestial colossus clothed in clouds, crowned with a rainbow and feet of burning fire
opt3: An eagle soaring above the crystal sea, holding an olive branch and a golden trumpet
opt4: And, lo, in the midst of the throne and of the four beasts, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes
correct: And, lo, in the midst of the throne and of the four beasts, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes
explanation: Instead of a roaring lion, John sees a sacrificial Lamb bearing the marks of slaughter, possessing seven horns (omnipotence) and seven eyes (omniscience/the seven Spirits of God). Revelation 5:6 (KJV) - "And I beheld, and, lo, in the midst of the throne and of the four beasts, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent forth into all the earth."

question: What did the four living creatures and the four and twenty elders hold when the Lamb took the book out of the right hand of Him on the throne?
opt1: Having every one of them harps, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints
opt2: Having crowns of silver, and iron bowls containing the ashes of martyrs
opt3: Having swords of brass, and wooden tablets inscribed with the sins of the world
opt4: Having palm branches, and silver trumpets prepared to announce the plagues
correct: Having every one of them harps, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints
explanation: The heavenly hosts worship with harps (praise) and golden incense bowls, which Scripture explicitly identifies as the accumulated prayers of God's saints. Revelation 5:8 (KJV) - "And when he had taken the book, the four beasts and four and twenty elders fell down before the Lamb, having every one of them harps, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints."

question: What new redemptive song did the heavenly hosts sing to celebrate the Lamb's worthiness in Revelation 5:9-10?
opt1: Thou art worthy: for Thou hast overthrown the Roman legions and established an earthly sanctuary in Jerusalem with gold
opt2: Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation; and hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth
opt3: Thou art worthy: for Thou hast calculated the numbers of the stars and measured the depths of the oceans of the earth
opt4: Thou art worthy: for Thou hast given the law on Mount Sinai and preserved the genealogies of the twelve tribes
correct: Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation; and hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth
explanation: The new song exalts the universal, blood-bought redemption achieved by Christ's sacrificial death, transforming believers from every global ethnicity into royal priests destined to reign on earth. Revelation 5:9-10 (KJV) - "And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation; And hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth."

question: How many angelic voices joined around the throne, and what sevenfold praise did they declare with a loud voice?
opt1: Twelve legions of angels; saying, Great is the monarch of heaven who overthroweth the idols of pagan Rome
opt2: Seven archangels; saying, Holy is the sanctuary of God which shineth above the clouds of the morning
opt3: The number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands; saying, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing
opt4: A company of four hundred elders; saying, Blessed is the seed of Abraham that inheriteth the land of Canaan
correct: The number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands; saying, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing
explanation: An innumerable angelic host numbering hundreds of millions unites in a thunderous sevenfold chorus of praise to the slain and exalted Lamb. Revelation 5:11-12 (KJV) - "And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands; Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing."

question: What universal cosmic doxology did John hear from every creature in heaven, earth, and sea in Revelation 5:13?
opt1: Tribute, and gold, and victory, be unto the armies of the saints who have fought valiantly on earth
opt2: Peace, and prosperity, and health, be multiplied unto all the inhabitants of the Roman province of Asia
opt3: Justice, and judgment, and vengeance, fall upon the persecutors who shed the blood of the prophets
opt4: Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever
correct: Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever
explanation: All created reality joins in unified worship, directing identical supreme praise, honor, and dominion to both the Father on the throne and the Lamb. Revelation 5:13 (KJV) - "And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever."

question: How did the four living creatures and the four and twenty elders conclude this celestial symphony of praise?
opt1: And the four beasts said, Amen. And the four and twenty elders fell down and worshipped him that liveth for ever and ever
opt2: And the four beasts sounded their trumpets, and the elders cast their harps into the crystal sea
opt3: And the four beasts drew their golden swords, and the elders marched out to battle the dragon
opt4: And the four beasts closed the heavenly door, and the elders sealed the book with an eighth seal
correct: And the four beasts said, Amen. And the four and twenty elders fell down and worshipped him that liveth for ever and ever
explanation: The grand liturgy of chapter 5 concludes with the cherubim's resounding 'Amen' and the elders prostrating in silent adoration before the eternal Lord. Revelation 5:14 (KJV) - "And the four beasts said, Amen. And the four and twenty elders fell down and worshipped him that liveth for ever and ever."

question: What divine prerogative did the Lamb exercise that demonstrated His equality with Him who sat upon the throne?
opt1: He commanded Michael to draft a new code of civil legislation for the Roman Empire
opt2: He came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat upon the throne
opt3: He instructed John to seal up the prophecy and bury the parchment under the altar
opt4: He cast down the four beasts and replaced them with four archangels of judgment
correct: He came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat upon the throne
explanation: The Lamb directly approaches the sovereign throne and takes the sealed scroll from the Father's hand, initiating the eschatological reclamation of the cosmos. Revelation 5:7 (KJV) - "And he came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat upon the throne."

question: When the Lamb opened the first seal, what horse and rider went forth, and what was given unto him?
opt1: A black horse with a rider holding a pair of balances in his hand to weigh barley
opt2: A red horse with a rider holding a great broadsword to take peace from the earth
opt3: And I saw, and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow; and a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer
opt4: A pale horse with a rider whose name was Death, and Hell followed after him
correct: And I saw, and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow; and a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer
explanation: The first seal unleashes a rider on a white horse armed with a bow, crowned as victor, riding forth in aggressive conquest. Revelation 6:2 (KJV) - "And I saw, and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow; and a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer."

question: What horse and mission were released when the Lamb opened the second seal in Revelation 6:3-4?
opt1: A spotted horse sent to destroy all commercial maritime vessels across the Mediterranean
opt2: A golden horse sent to distribute municipal prosperity and peace among Roman provinces
opt3: A dark horse sent to bring drought upon the vineyards and olive orchards of Asia
opt4: Another horse that was red: and power was given to him that sat thereon to take peace from the earth, and that they should kill one another: and there was given unto him a great sword
correct: Another horse that was red: and power was given to him that sat thereon to take peace from the earth, and that they should kill one another: and there was given unto him a great sword
explanation: The second seal depicts a fiery red horse representing widespread slaughter, civil warfare, and the removal of peace from the earth through a great sword. Revelation 6:4 (KJV) - "And there went out another horse that was red: and power was given to him that sat thereon to take peace from the earth, and that they should kill one another: and there was given unto him a great sword."

question: When the third seal was opened, what horse appeared, and what voice concerning scarcity did John hear?
opt1: And I beheld, and lo a black horse; and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand. And I heard a voice say, A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny; and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine
opt2: A white horse whose rider threw bags of gold into the marketplace, declaring that famine was ended
opt3: A red horse whose rider burned all granaries, declaring that bread would never again be baked
opt4: A pale horse whose rider poisoned the wells, declaring that pure water would cost ten silver coins
correct: And I beheld, and lo a black horse; and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand. And I heard a voice say, A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny; and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine
explanation: The black horse symbolizes acute economic inflation and food scarcity, where a day's wage (a denarius/penny) purchases merely one day's basic sustenance, while luxury oil and wine are spared. Revelation 6:5-6 (KJV) - "And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third beast say, Come and see. And I beheld, and lo a black horse; and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand. And I heard a voice in the midst of the four beasts say, A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny; and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine."

question: Who rode the pale horse released at the fourth seal, and over what portion of the earth was authority granted?
opt1: His name was Apollyon, and power was given to burn one third of the forests and rivers
opt2: His name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth
opt3: His name was Belial, and power was given to overturn the thrones of half the kings of the Gentiles
opt4: His name was Lucifer, and power was given to strike down the priests of the temple with sudden leprosy
correct: His name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth
explanation: The fourth seal releases Death and Hades on a sickly pale horse, exercising lethal jurisdiction over a quarter of the globe through war, famine, pestilence, and wild beasts. Revelation 6:8 (KJV) - "And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth."

question: What did John see beneath the altar when the fifth seal was opened in Revelation 6:9-10?
opt1: The bodies of the twenty-four elders weeping because their earthly cities had been destroyed
opt2: The spirits of rebellious angels begging for pardon from the chains of darkness
opt3: The souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: and they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?
opt4: The ashes of sacrificial bulls and goats offered during the annual day of atonement
correct: The souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: and they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?
explanation: Martyred saints are seen beneath heaven's sacrificial altar, petitioning God's righteous justice to vindicate their spilled blood upon persecuting earthly dwellers. Revelation 6:9-10 (KJV) - "And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?"

question: What was given unto these martyred souls under the altar, and what instruction were they told to await?
opt1: Golden swords were given unto them, and they were told to descend immediately to destroy Roman legions
opt2: Crowns of laurels were given unto them, and they were told to govern the twelve tribes of Israel
opt3: Silver harps were given unto them, and they were told to cease from intercession forever
opt4: White robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled
correct: White robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled
explanation: The martyrs receive robes of victory and righteousness, instructed to rest patiently until the predetermined full number of fellow martyrs is completed. Revelation 6:11 (KJV) - "And white robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled."

question: What cataclysmic cosmic convulsions shook the physical universe when the sixth seal was opened?
opt1: Lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood; and the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, and the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together
opt2: A flood of boiling water covered all mountain ranges, and the oceans froze into blocks of solid ice
opt3: A shower of gold coins rained upon the Roman senate, and the palaces of Caesar dissolved into smoke
opt4: A plague of fiery serpents bit the merchants of Asia, and the Mediterranean sea turned into fresh milk
correct: Lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood; and the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, and the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together
explanation: The sixth seal triggers universal celestial and terrestrial disruptions: massive earthquake, solar eclipse like sackcloth, blood-red moon, meteor storms, and the skies receding like a rolled scroll.
