opt1: Extinguish the fire of the altar and cast the golden censer into the sea
opt2: Dispatch Michael to overthrow the thrones of the kings of the northern wilderness
opt3: Loose the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates
opt4: Seal the gates of the heavenly temple and summon the twenty-four elders to war
correct: Loose the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates
explanation: A voice from the golden altar commands the sixth angel to release four high-ranking demonic princes long held bound at the ancient boundary of the river Euphrates. Revelation 9:13-14 (KJV) - "And the sixth angel sounded, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is before God, Saying to the sixth angel which had the trumpet, Loose the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates."

question: For what precise time were these four angels prepared, and what lethality did they unleash upon humanity?
opt1: Prepared for three weeks of drought to dry up all the rivers of Asia Minor
opt2: Prepared for seven years of famine to consume the storehouses of Egypt and Rome
opt3: Prepared for forty days of pestilence to strike down the rulers of the Gentiles
opt4: Prepared for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year, for to slay the third part of men
correct: Prepared for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year, for to slay the third part of men
explanation: These demonic destroyers were reserved for an exact, divinely appointed moment in history to slaughter one-third of the human race. Revelation 9:15 (KJV) - "And the four angels were loosed, which were prepared for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year, for to slay the third part of men."

question: What was the staggering number of the horsemen army, and what issued out of the mouths of the horses?
opt1: The number of the army of the horsemen were two hundred thousand thousand; and out of their mouths issued fire and smoke and brimstone
opt2: Ten thousand times ten thousand cavalry; and out of their mouths issued boiling water and hail
opt3: One hundred and forty-four thousand warriors; and out of their mouths issued sharp iron arrows
opt4: Twelve legions of horsemen; and out of their mouths issued venomous serpents and scorpions
correct: The number of the army of the horsemen were two hundred thousand thousand; and out of their mouths issued fire and smoke and brimstone
explanation: The invading demonic horde numbers 200 million (two hundred thousand thousand), whose lion-headed mounts slay one-third of humanity through three deadly plagues: fire, smoke, and brimstone. Revelation 9:16-18 (KJV) - "And the number of the army of the horsemen were two hundred thousand thousand: and I heard the number of them. And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and them that sat on them, having breastplates of fire, and of jacinth, and brimstone: and the heads of the horses were as the heads of lions; and out of their mouths issued fire and smoke and brimstone. By these three was the third part of men killed, by the fire, and by the smoke, and by the brimstone, which issued out of their mouths."

question: Despite these catastrophic plagues that wiped out a third of mankind, what shocking obstinacy characterized the rest of men?
opt1: They immediately tore their garments in sackcloth and ashes, turning wholeheartedly unto the God of heaven
opt2: Yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts
opt3: They dismantled all pagan shrines throughout Rome and enacted biblical legislation across all provinces
opt4: They surrendered all weapons of war and pooled their material wealth to support surviving orphans
correct: Yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts
explanation: The survivors displayed hardened, impenitent defiance, refusing to abandon demon worship, lifeless idolatry, murder, the occult (sorceries/pharmakeia), sexual immorality, and theft. Revelation 9:20-21 (KJV) - "And the rest of the men which were not killed by these plagues yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: which neither can see, nor hear, nor walk: Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts."

question: How does John describe the glorious appearance of the mighty angel descending from heaven in Revelation 10:1?
opt1: Wearing armor of iron, with a helmet of bronze, and holding an eagle standard of Roman legions
opt2: Adorned in priestly garments of white linen, with the breastplate of Urim and Thummim
opt3: Clothed with a cloud: and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was as it were the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire
opt4: Surrounded by a dense mist of black smoke, with wings of an eagle and eyes of burning coal
correct: Clothed with a cloud: and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was as it were the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire
explanation: A colossal mighty angel appears reflecting divine attributes: robed in a cloud, crowned with a rainbow covenant, radiant like the sun, with blazing pillar-like feet. Revelation 10:1 (KJV) - "And I saw another mighty angel come down from heaven, clothed with a cloud: and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was as it were the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire:"

question: What object did the mighty angel hold in his hand, and how did he place his feet upon the cosmos?
opt1: He held a golden scepter: and placed both feet upon the peaks of Mount Zion in Jerusalem
opt2: He held a silver trumpet: and hovered suspended in the clouds above the island of Patmos
opt3: He held a balance of scales: and stood upon the battlements of the imperial palace of Rome
opt4: He had in his hand a little book open: and he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left foot on the earth
correct: He had in his hand a little book open: and he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left foot on the earth
explanation: Holding an unsealed little scroll, the angel plants his right foot on the sea and his left on dry land, asserting sovereign divine authority over the entire globe. Revelation 10:2 (KJV) - "And he had in his hand a little book open: and he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left foot on the earth,"

question: When the mighty angel cried as when a lion roareth, what celestial voices uttered their speech?
opt1: Seven thunders uttered their voices
opt2: Twelve trumpets sounded their alarms
opt3: Four living creatures sang their praises
opt4: Twenty-four elders fell upon their faces
correct: Seven thunders uttered their voices
explanation: The angel's lion-like roar triggers the thunderous utterances of seven distinct heavenly voices. Revelation 10:3 (KJV) - "And cried with a loud voice, as when a lion roareth: and when he had cried, seven thunders uttered their voices."

question: What divine prohibition was given to John as he was about to write down what the seven thunders uttered?
opt1: Write them immediately upon tablets of bronze and send them to the Roman senate
opt2: I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Seal up those things which the seven thunders uttered, and write them not
opt3: Translate them into Hebrew and Greek and proclaim them in every synagogue of Asia
opt4: Carve them upon the rocks of the island of Patmos for future generations of pilgrims
correct: I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Seal up those things which the seven thunders uttered, and write them not
explanation: God sovereignly conceals the specific revelation of the seven thunders, instructing John to seal them unwritten, reminding believers that some divine mysteries remain unrevealed. Revelation 10:4 (KJV) - "And when the seven thunders had uttered their voices, I was about to write: and I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Seal up those things which the seven thunders uttered, and write them not."

question: What solemn oath did the mighty angel swear by the eternal Creator while lifting his hand to heaven?
opt1: Sware by the blood of the martyrs, that the empire of Rome would fall within ten days
opt2: Sware by the throne of David, that the physical temple of Jerusalem would be restored in gold
opt3: Sware by him that liveth for ever and ever, who created heaven, and the things that therein are, that there should be time no longer
opt4: Sware by the archangel Michael, that the plagues of the earth would be suspended for a millennium
correct: Sware by him that liveth for ever and ever, who created heaven, and the things that therein are, that there should be time no longer
explanation: Lifting his hand to heaven, the angel swears by the eternal Creator that there will be no more delay ('time no longer') in the execution of God's final purposes. Revelation 10:5-6 (KJV) - "And the angel which I saw stand upon the sea and upon the earth lifted up his hand to heaven, And sware by him that liveth for ever and ever, who created heaven, and the things that therein are, and the earth, and the things that therein are, and the sea, and the things which are therein, that there should be time no longer:"

question: When will the mystery of God be completely finished according to Revelation 10:7?
opt1: When the Roman legions lay down their arms and acknowledge the gospel before all nations
opt2: When the four winds of the earth are permanently dissolved and creation ceases to exist
opt3: When the elders of the church in Ephesus restore their first love and rebuild the altars
opt4: In the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets
correct: In the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets
explanation: The sounding of the seventh trumpet marks the final consummation of God's redemptive mystery as foretold throughout the Old Testament prophetic Scriptures. Revelation 10:7 (KJV) - "But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets."

question: What command did the heavenly voice give John concerning the little book held by the angel?
opt1: Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel which standeth upon the sea and upon the earth
opt2: Bow down before the angel and ask him to interpret the seven seals of prophecy
opt3: Cast the little book into the Mediterranean sea that its words may be hidden from men
opt4: Take the little book and place it beside the golden censer on the altar of incense
correct: Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel which standeth upon the sea and upon the earth
explanation: John is instructed to personally approach the mighty angel and take possession of the open scroll. Revelation 10:8 (KJV) - "And the voice which I heard from heaven spake unto me again, and said, Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel which standeth upon the sea and upon the earth."

question: What sensory effect did the little book produce when John ate it according to the angel's instruction?
opt1: It tasted like bitter wormwood in the mouth, but produced sweet joy and peace in the belly
opt2: It was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter
opt3: It burned his lips like coals of fire, and filled his heart with miraculous prophetic tongues
opt4: It refreshed his soul like pure milk and wine, leaving no sensation of sorrow or bitterness
correct: It was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter
explanation: God's Word is inherently sweet to receive, but internalizing its sobering prophecies of cosmic judgment and doom produces profound inner grief and bitterness. Revelation 10:9-10 (KJV) - "And I went unto the angel, and said unto him, Give me the little book. And he said unto me, Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey. And I took the little book out of the angel's hand, and ate it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter."

question: What renewed prophetic commission was laid upon John after digesting the little book?
opt1: Thou must return immediately to Ephesus and assume the episcopal oversight of all assemblies
opt2: Thou must seal thy lips in perpetual silence and write no more concerning the end of the age
opt3: Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings
opt4: Thou must construct a physical sanctuary on the island of Patmos to shelter fleeing disciples
correct: Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings
explanation: Eating the scroll re-commissions John for a wider prophetic ministry directed toward global peoples, ethnic nations, varied languages, and earthly rulers. Revelation 10:11 (KJV) - "And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings."

question: To what did the angel's voice compare when he cried out in Revelation 10:3?
opt1: As the sound of many rushing waters
opt2: As the crashing of a violent thunderstorm
opt3: As the blast of a thousand silver trumpets
opt4: As when a lion roareth
correct: As when a lion roareth
explanation: The voice of the mighty angel reverberated with the authoritative, terrifying power of a roaring lion. Revelation 10:3 (KJV) - "And cried with a loud voice, as when a lion roareth: and when he had cried, seven thunders uttered their voices."

question: What measuring instrument was given to John, and what was he commanded to measure and to leave out?
opt1: There was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein. But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles
opt2: A golden cord: and he was commanded to measure the walls of Rome, but leave out the harbor
opt3: An iron chain: and he was commanded to measure the caves of Patmos, but leave out the sea
opt4: A silver line: and he was commanded to measure the streets of Babylon, but leave out the palaces
correct: There was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein. But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles
explanation: John is instructed to measure God's sanctuary, altar, and true worshipers (signifying divine ownership and protection), while excluding the outer court given over to Gentile desecration. Revelation 11:1-2 (KJV) - "And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein. But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months."

question: How long will the holy city be trodden under foot by the Gentiles according to Revelation 11:2?
opt1: Seventy weeks of years
opt2: Forty and two months
opt3: Ten literal days
opt4: Three hundred and sixty days
correct: Forty and two months
explanation: The period of Gentile oppression of Jerusalem is specified as 42 months (3.5 years / 1,260 days). Revelation 11:2 (KJV) - "But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months."

question: How long will God's two witnesses prophesy, and in what attire will they minister?
opt1: Five hundred days, clothed in white linen
opt2: Seventy days, clothed in armor of iron
opt3: A thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth
opt4: One hundred and twenty days, clothed in robes of purple
correct: A thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth
explanation: The two witnesses proclaim divine truth for 1,260 days (a thousand two hundred and threescore days), wearing sackcloth to symbolize national mourning and repentance. Revelation 11:3 (KJV) - "And I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth."

question: How are the two witnesses symbolically identified, and what miraculous defensive power protects them?
opt1: These are the two cherubim of gold, and whoever approaches them is struck down with sudden leprosy
opt2: These are the two pillars of the temple, and whoever strikes them is crushed by falling stones
opt3: These are the two archangels of heaven, and whoever opposes them is blinded by lightning
opt4: These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth. And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies
correct: These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth. And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies
explanation: Echoing Zechariah 4, they are the two olive trees and lampstands; adversaries attempting to harm them are consumed by fire proceeding from their mouths. Revelation 11:4-5 (KJV) - "These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth. And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies: and if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed."

question: What supernatural powers over nature are possessed by the two witnesses during the days of their prophecy?
opt1: These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will
opt2: Power to move mountain ranges into the sea and command angelic cavalry to overthrow empires
opt3: Power to turn stones into bread and multiply physical gold for the impoverished assemblies
opt4: Power to walk on water and calm oceanic tempests during Mediterranean trading voyages
correct: These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will
explanation: Demonstrating powers reminiscent of Elijah and Moses, they can withhold rain, turn waters into blood, and strike the earth with plagues at will. Revelation 11:6 (KJV) - "These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will."

question: When they finish their testimony, who attacks and slays the two witnesses, and where do their dead bodies lie unburied?
opt1: The emperor of Rome shall execute them, and their bodies shall be cast into the Tiber river
opt2: The beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them. And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified
opt3: The Sanhedrin elders shall stone them, and their bodies shall be buried outside the Damascus gate
opt4: The false prophet of Babylon shall poison them, and their bodies shall be burned upon pagan altars
correct: The beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them. And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified
explanation: The Beast rising from the abyss martyres them once their mission is finished, leaving their corpses exposed in Jerusalem ('spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified'). Revelation 11:7-8 (KJV) - "And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them. And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified."

question: How do earth's inhabitants gloat over the dead witnesses, and what dramatic resurrection occurs after three days and a half?
opt1: They mourn in sackcloth for forty days until angelic chariots descend to bury them in secret
opt2: They build marble monuments over them, but lightning from heaven dissolves the tombs into dust
opt3: They that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another... And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them
opt4: They offer sacrifices to the Beast, until an earthquake swallows the entire province into the abyss
correct: They that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another... And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them
explanation: The ungodly world celebrates their deaths by exchanging gifts, but after three and a half days, God's breath resurrects them, striking terror into onlookers. Revelation 11:10-11 (KJV) - "And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth. And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them."

question: What voice from heaven summoned the resurrected witnesses, and what seismic catastrophe shook the city immediately?
opt1: A voice cried, Descend into the abyss: and an earthquake split the Mount of Olives into four rivers
opt2: A voice cried, Slay your enemies: and fire consumed forty thousand Roman soldiers in the garrison
opt3: A voice cried, Build the temple: and a tenth part of the city was transformed into golden palaces
opt4: They heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them. And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand
correct: They heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them. And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand
explanation: Called upward by God, they ascend in a cloud before their enemies' eyes, followed immediately by an earthquake that destroys a tenth of Jerusalem and slays 7,000 notable individuals. Revelation 11:12-13 (KJV) - "And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them. And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven."

question: What glorious proclamation echoed in heaven when the seventh angel sounded his trumpet in Revelation 11:15?
opt1: The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever
opt2: The armies of the nations have defeated the Roman empire, and human liberty is established on earth
opt3: The temple of Jerusalem has been restored in marble, and the sacrifices of Aaron shall never cease
opt4: The stars of the heavens have ceased their orbits, and eternal silence has overtaken creation
correct: The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever
explanation: The seventh trumpet announces the ultimate sovereign victory: all earthly dominion is transferred forever to God and His Messiah. Revelation 11:15 (KJV) - "And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever."

question: What heavenly scene was unveiled at the conclusion of chapter 11 when God's temple was opened in heaven?
opt1: The gates of the abyss were opened, and Lucifer ascended with seven thousand demons of darkness
opt2: And the temple of God was opened in heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: and there were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail
opt3: The throne of Solomon was brought forth, and the kings of the Gentiles bowed before golden altars
opt4: The sea of glass dissolved into blood, and the twenty-four elders cast their white robes into the fire
correct: And the temple of God was opened in heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: and there were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail
explanation: Heaven's temple is opened, revealing the Ark of the Covenant (sign of God's faithful presence and covenant keeping), accompanied by thunderous cosmic manifestations. Revelation 11:19 (KJV) - "And the temple of God was opened in heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: and there were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail."

question: What great wonder appeared in heaven in Revelation 12:1 depicting a radiant woman?
opt1: A queen clothed in imperial purple, holding a golden scepter and sitting on the seven hills of Rome
opt2: A prophetess clothed in sackcloth, weeping over the ruins of the temple of Jerusalem
opt3: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars
opt4: An empress adorned with diamonds and pearls, commanding an earthly cavalry of horsemen
correct: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars
explanation: John sees a celestial sign: a woman robed in the brilliance of the sun, the moon beneath her feet, and crowned with twelve stars representing the twelve tribes of Israel. Revelation 12:1 (KJV) - "And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars:"

question: How does John describe the second wonder in heaven, the great red dragon, in Revelation 12:3-4?
opt1: A black serpent having four heads and twelve horns, whose breath poisoned all the fresh waters of the earth
opt2: A winged leopard having three heads and six horns, whose claws broke the pillars of the temple
opt3: A monstrous leviathan having ten heads and twenty horns, whose roar shook the foundations of the mountains
opt4: A great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads. And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth
correct: A great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads. And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth
explanation: The adversary is revealed as a colossal fiery red dragon having seven crowned heads, ten horns, and a tail sweeping down a third of heaven's stars (rebellious angels). Revelation 12:3-4 (KJV) - "And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads. And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born."

question: What destiny and divine rescue awaited the man child brought forth by the woman?
opt1: She brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne
opt2: She brought forth an earthly king who conquered the Roman legions and established an earthly dynasty in Judea
opt3: She brought forth a high priest who restored the daily sacrifices of the temple in Jerusalem
opt4: She brought forth a celestial prophet who remained hidden in the wilderness caves of Arabia
correct: She brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne
explanation: The male child is the messianic Ruler destined to govern all nations with a rod of iron (Psalm 2), who was caught up through His ascension to God's sovereign throne. Revelation 12:5 (KJV) - "And she brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne."

question: Where did the woman flee after the ascension of her child, and for how long was she nourished there?
opt1: The woman fled into the island of Patmos, where she was hidden for forty-two weeks
opt2: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days
opt3: The woman fled into the mountains of Media, where she was guarded for seventy literal days
opt4: The woman fled into the city of Babylon, where she was sheltered for three hundred days
correct: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days
explanation: God provides a secure wilderness refuge for the woman where she is divinely sustained for 1,260 days (a thousand two hundred and threescore days / 3.5 prophetic years). Revelation 12:6 (KJV) - "And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days."

question: What cosmic conflict erupted in heaven, and who was cast down to the earth?
opt1: Gabriel and his legions fought against the Beast of the sea, and drowned his armies in the crystal sea
opt2: The twenty-four elders drew their swords against Apollyon, and bound him in the river Euphrates
opt3: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels, and prevailed not... and the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world
opt4: The martyred saints fought against the Roman emperors, and overthrew the thrones of the Gentiles
correct: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels, and prevailed not... and the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world
explanation: Heaven is purged as Michael's angelic hosts defeat Satan and his demonic angels, hurling that ancient serpent, the Devil, permanently down to the terrestrial realm. Revelation 12:7-9 (KJV) - "And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels, And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven. And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him."

question: What title does the loud voice in heaven assign to Satan when rejoicing over his expulsion?
opt1: The monarch of earthly kings, who governed the municipal assemblies of Asia
opt2: The ruler of the air, who commanded the storms of the Mediterranean sea
opt3: The prince of Tartarus, who held the golden keys of the bottomless pit
opt4: The accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night
correct: The accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night
explanation: Satan's malicious role as the relentless prosecutor of the saints before God is forever terminated by his ejection from heaven. question: What appearance and deceptive speech characterized the second beast rising out of the earth in Revelation 13:11?

question: How were the seven angels bearing the seven plagues robed when they came out of the temple?
opt1: Clothed in scarlet armor of bronze, and having helmets of iron crowned with pearls
opt2: Clothed in pure and white linen, and having their breasts girded with golden girdles

Revelation 15:6 (KJV) - "And the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues, clothed in pure and white linen, and having their breasts girded with golden girdles."

question: Who delivered the seven golden vials full of the wrath of God unto the seven angels?

question: What filled the temple of God, and what limitation was placed upon entry until the plagues were fulfilled?

explanation: The Shekinah glory and omnipotence fill the temple with dense smoke (echoing Exodus 40 and 1 Kings 8), temporarily suspending all priestly intercession until judgment is accomplished. Revelation 15:8 (KJV) - "And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God, and from his power; and no man was able to enter into the temple, till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled."

question: Over what four aspects of the Beast's demonic system had the standing saints on the sea of glass gotten the victory?

Revelation 15:2 (KJV) - "And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass, having the harps of God."

question: What title is ascribed to the Lord God Almighty in the Song of the Lamb in Revelation 15:3?

opt4: Thou Architect of Worlds

question: What painful physical plague broke out when the first angel poured his vial upon the earth?
opt1: Sudden blindness struck all municipal magistrates and Roman soldiers throughout Asia Minor

opt3: There fell a noisome and grievous sore upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image

explanation: The first bowl unleashes malignant, agonizing ulcerous sores exclusively upon those bearing the mark of the Beast and worshiping his image. Revelation 16:2 (KJV) - "And the first went, and poured out his vial upon the earth; and there fell a noisome and grievous sore upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image."

question: What oceanic catastrophe occurred upon the pouring of the second vial in Revelation 16:3?
opt1: The sea dried up into dry sand, and all commercial merchant ships were stranded upon the rocks

explanation: Unlike the partial second trumpet, the second bowl turns the entire ocean into coagulated, putrid blood like that of a corpse, exterminating all marine life. Revelation 16:3 (KJV) - "And the second angel poured out his vial upon the sea; and it became as the blood of a dead man: and every living soul died in the sea."

question: What transformation struck fresh water sources at the third vial, and how did the angel of the waters justify God's judgment?
opt1: Poured out his vial upon the rivers and fountains of waters; and they became blood. And I heard the angel of the waters say, Thou art righteous, O Lord... because thou hast judged thus. opt2: Poured his vial upon the springs and they turned to bitter wormwood, and the angel said, God hath spared the righteous from thirst

opt4: Poured his vial upon the fountains and they froze to ice, and the angel said, God hath halted the travel of the wicked

For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and thou hast given them blood to drink; for they are worthy
explanation: All drinking water turns to blood in exact lex talionis retribution: because persecutors shed the blood of saints and prophets, God compels them to drink blood. Revelation 16:4-6 (KJV) - "And the third angel poured out his vial upon the rivers and fountains of waters; and they became blood. And I heard the angel of the waters say, Thou art righteous, O Lord, which art, and wast, and shalt be, because thou hast judged thus. For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and thou hast given them blood to drink; for they are worthy."

question: What solar affliction resulted from the pouring of the fourth vial, and how did afflicted mankind respond?
opt1: The sun was completely extinguished into darkness, and men wept in sackcloth seeking divine pardon

opt3: The sun produced gentle warmth, and men celebrated feasts of thanksgiving across all provinces
opt4: The sun rained down gold dust, and men worshiped the emperors in civic forums

explanation: Intense solar radiation scorches humanity with fierce heat, yet instead of repenting, hardened sinners blaspheme the sovereign God who controls the plagues. Revelation 16:8-9 (KJV) - "And the fourth angel poured out his vial upon the sun; and power was given unto him to scorch men with fire. question: What occurred when the sixth angel poured his vial upon the great river Euphrates?

question: What came out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet, and what is their mission?

explanation: Demonic frog-like spirits proceed from the satanic triumvirate, working deceptive wonders to muster global rulers for the final conflict against God. question: Where does the demonic deception assemble the kings of the whole world for this climactic battle?

explanation: The global armies converge at Har-Magedon (the Mount of Megiddo in northern Israel), the historic stage for decisive apocalyptic battle. Revelation 16:16 (KJV) - "And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon."

question: What thunderous proclamation issued from the heavenly temple when the seventh angel poured his vial into the air?

Revelation 16:17 (KJV) - "And the seventh angel poured out his vial into the air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, It is done."

question: What unprecedented earthquake and aerial plague struck the earth under the seventh vial in Revelation 16:18-21?
opt1: A shower of volcanic ash that buried all the seven churches of Asia Minor under thirty cubits of stone

explanation: The greatest earthquake in human history splits Babylon into three parts, levels global cities, causes islands and mountains to vanish, and drops 100-pound hailstones upon blaspheming men. Revelation 16:18-21 (KJV) - "And there were voices, and thunders, and lightnings; and there was a great earthquake, such as was not since men were upon the earth, so mighty an earthquake, and so great. question: How does the angel describe the judgment shown to John in the opening of Revelation 17?

opt4: Come hither; I will show thee the resurrection of the ancient kings of Israel from their sepulchres

explanation: One of the vial-bearing angels invites John to witness the condemnation of the apostate global religious system, personified as a seductive harlot riding upon corrupt nations. Revelation 17:1-2 (KJV) - "And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters: With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication."

question: What beast was the woman sitting upon when John was carried away in the Spirit into the wilderness?

opt4: A golden chariot drawn by four fiery lions, driven by the false prophet of Rome

explanation: The harlot rides upon the scarlet-colored political Beast (Antichrist system), saturated with blasphemous titles, possessing seven heads and ten horns. Revelation 17:3 (KJV) - "So he carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns."

question: How was the woman arrayed, and what cup did she hold in her hand in Revelation 17:4?

opt4: Arrayed in armor of iron, and holding an eagle standard, having a bronze horn full of oil

explanation: She is decked in opulent royal colors (purple and scarlet) and ostentatious jewelry, wielding a golden cup overflowing with spiritual abominations and idolatry. Revelation 17:4 (KJV) - "And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication:"

question: What enigmatic title was written upon the forehead of this woman in Revelation 17:5?

Revelation 17:5 (KJV) - "And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH."

Revelation 17:6 (KJV) - "And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: and when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration."

question: How does the angel explain the mysterious paradox of the Beast that John saw in Revelation 17:8?
opt1: The beast that thou sawest was created in Eden, and fell into the sea, and shall reign on earth for a thousand years

opt4: The beast that thou sawest was an angel of heaven, and became mortal, and shall build a temple in Babylon

explanation: The Beast's trajectory parodies God's eternal nature: he was, is not, will ascend from the abyss, and is destined for ultimate destruction (perdition). Revelation 17:8 (KJV) - "The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition: and they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, when they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is."

question: What is the mind which hath wisdom regarding the seven heads of the Beast?

Revelation 17:9-10 (KJV) - "And here is the mind which hath wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sitteth. question: Who are the ten horns on the Beast, and what unified power do they give unto him?

explanation: The ten horns are future allied rulers who reign briefly alongside the Beast, voluntarily subordinating their military and political sovereignty to his control. Revelation 17:12-13 (KJV) - "And the ten horns which thou sawest are ten kings, which have received no kingdom as yet; but receive power as kings one hour with the beast. These have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast."

question: What will happen when these ten kings and the Beast make war with the Lamb?

Revelation 17:14 (KJV) - "These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful."

question: What violent turning against the harlot occurs among the ten horns and the Beast according to Revelation 17:16-17?

opt4: They shall send her ambassadors to all nations, and enforce her religious liturgy by civil law

explanation: The political beast system turns savagely upon its religious rider, stripping, devouring, and incinerating her, fulfilling God's sovereign providential plan. question: What mighty proclamation did an angel descending with great power declare regarding Babylon in Revelation 18:2?

explanation: A radiant angel announces the final, absolute devastation of commercial and political Babylon, reduced to a desolate haunt of demons and unclean spirits. Revelation 18:2 (KJV) - "And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird."

question: What urgent pastoral command did a voice from heaven address to God's people residing in Babylon?
opt1: Remain within her walls, my people, that ye may convert her merchants and reform her laws

opt4: Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues

Revelation 18:4 (KJV) - "And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues."

question: With what speed and certainty will divine retribution overtake proud Babylon according to Revelation 18:8?

opt4: Her demise shall occur through seasonal droughts spreading slowly across forty decades: for silent is the judgment upon her

explanation: Babylon's boastful self-confidence ('I sit a queen, and am no widow') is shattered by sudden annihilation occurring in a single day under God's irresistible power. Revelation 18:8 (KJV) - "Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her."

question: Why do the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over the desolation of Babylon in Revelation 18:11?
