opt3: Merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls... and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men
opt4: Merchandise of cinnamon, odours, ointments, frankincense... and sheep, cattle, and goats
correct: Merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls... and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men
explanation: The catalog of commerce reveals the predatory heart of Babylon's consumerism, degrading human beings created in God's image into commodities: 'slaves, and souls of men.' Revelation 18:12-13 (KJV) - "The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all manner vessels of ivory, and all manner vessels of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble, And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men."

question: How do shipmasters and sea merchants react as they watch the smoke of Babylon's burning from afar?
opt1: They cheered with joy and set sail to establish new commercial monopolies in the harbors of Greece
opt2: They launched rescue boats with buckets of sea water to extinguish the flames of the harbor palaces
opt3: They sailed into the mouth of the Tiber river and surrendered their vessels to Roman authorities
opt4: They cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate
correct: They cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate
explanation: Maritime traders stand traumatized at sea, casting dust upon their heads in sorrow over the swift, total obliteration of their economic benefactor. Revelation 18:17-19 (KJV) - "And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city! And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate."

question: What summons to heavenly rejoicing is sounded over the downfall of Babylon in Revelation 18:20?
opt1: Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her
opt2: Mourn over her, ye saints, for the glory of human civilization has perished from the earth
opt3: Weep over her, ye angels, for the sanctuary of marble has been dissolved into black ash
opt4: Fast over her, ye elders, for forty days in sackcloth before the presence of the throne
correct: Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her
explanation: Heaven, apostles, and prophets are called to holy jubilation because God has executed righteous judgment and avenged the blood of His persecuted saints. Revelation 18:20 (KJV) - "Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her."

question: What dramatic symbolic action did a mighty angel perform to depict the violent and irrevocable destruction of Babylon?
opt1: Took a flaming torch from the altar, and hurled it upon the hills of Rome, saying, Thus shall fire consume her
opt2: A mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all
opt3: Took an iron rod, and shattered a potter's vessel upon the pavement, saying, Thus shall her people be broken
opt4: Took a golden trumpet, and blew a blast that leveled the city walls, saying, Thus shall her towers collapse
correct: A mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all
explanation: A mighty angel hurls a massive millstone into the ocean, vividly illustrating the sudden, violent, and permanent plunge of Babylon into oblivion. Revelation 18:21 (KJV) - "And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all."

question: What complete cessation of cultural, industrial, and social life is cataloged in Babylon's ruins in Revelation 18:22-23?
opt1: The debates of philosophers, the recitations of poets, the decrees of senators, and the trade of merchants
opt2: The morning sacrifices of priests, the chants of levites, the readings of scribes, and the blowing of shofars
opt3: The voice of harpers, and musicians, and of pipers, and trumpeters, shall be heard no more at all in thee; and no craftsman... and the sound of a millstone... and the light of a candle... and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride
opt4: The marching of legions, the forging of shields, the drilling of cavalry, and the shouts of centurions
correct: The voice of harpers, and musicians, and of pipers, and trumpeters, shall be heard no more at all in thee; and no craftsman... and the sound of a millstone... and the light of a candle... and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride
explanation: Music, craftsmanship, daily labor, domestic light, and joyful wedding celebrations are extinguished forever in the silence of Babylon's desolation. Revelation 18:22-23 (KJV) - "And the voice of harpers, and musicians, and of pipers, and trumpeters, shall be heard no more at all in thee; and no craftsman, of whatsoever craft he be, shall be found any more in thee; and the sound of a millstone shall be heard no more at all in thee; And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee: for thy merchants were the great men of the earth; for by thy sorceries were all nations deceived."

question: What ultimate indictment is laid upon Babylon in the concluding verse of Revelation 18?
opt1: And in her was found the accumulated stolen gold and silver of all the temples of the Orient
opt2: And in her was found the secret treaties forged between the kings of the earth and the dragon
opt3: And in her was found the unburied corpses of seventy thousand Roman soldiers fallen in Asia
opt4: And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth
correct: And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth
explanation: Babylon bears the corporate guilt for the martyred blood of all God's prophets, saints, and righteous individuals throughout human history. Revelation 18:24 (KJV) - "And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth."

question: What thunderous fourfold Hallelujah echoes through heaven in the opening verses of Revelation 19 celebrating God's judgment on the great whore?
opt1: Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God: for true and righteous are his judgments: for he hath judged the great whore
opt2: Hosanna; Peace, and prosperity, and dominion, be multiplied unto the churches of the province of Asia
opt3: Amen; The temple of Jerusalem is rebuilt, and the sacrifices of the law shall be celebrated forever
opt4: Holy; The archangels have conquered the legions of Caesar, and the earth is delivered from taxation
correct: Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God: for true and righteous are his judgments: for he hath judged the great whore
explanation: Heaven erupts into the first of four triumphant 'Alleluias' praising God's justice, holiness, and true judgment in avenging His servants upon the corrupt harlot. Revelation 19:1-2 (KJV) - "And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God: For true and righteous are his judgments: for he hath judged the great whore, which did corrupt the earth with her fornication, and hath avenged the blood of his servants at her hand."

question: What triumphant reason for rejoicing is proclaimed by the voice of a great multitude as the sound of many waters in Revelation 19:6-7?
opt1: Alleluia: for the kings of the Gentiles have surrendered their swords to the twelve apostles of Israel
opt2: Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth. Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready
opt3: Alleluia: for the physical temple on Mount Zion has descended with gates of pearl and walls of jasper
opt4: Alleluia: for the mortal bodies of believers have been endowed with wings of silver to explore the stars
correct: Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth. Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready
explanation: A roaring celestial chorus celebrates the sovereign reign of the omnipotent Lord God and announces the long-awaited Marriage of the Lamb to His prepared bride. Revelation 19:6-7 (KJV) - "And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth. Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready."

question: How was the Lamb's wife arrayed for her wedding, and what does this garment represent?
opt1: Arrayed in purple and scarlet robes embroidered with gold and pearls, representing civic authority
opt2: Arrayed in garments of sackcloth and camel's hair, representing the austerity of the prophets
opt3: To her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints
opt4: Arrayed in imperial armor of brass and silver, representing martial victory over Roman armies
correct: To her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints
explanation: The bride's wedding attire is pure, dazzling white linen, explicitly interpreted as the righteous deeds and imputed righteousness of the saints. Revelation 19:8 (KJV) - "And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints."

question: When John fell at the feet of the angel to worship him, how did the angel rebuke him and define prophecy?
opt1: Arise, for I am Michael the archangel, and thou art worthy to share in my celestial authority
opt2: Bow down again, for I bear the golden signet of the Father, and command the hosts of heaven
opt3: Weep not, for an angel may receive reverence from mortals who dwell in the wilderness of Patmos
opt4: See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy
correct: See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy
explanation: The angel firmly directs all worship exclusively to God, identifying himself as a fellow servant and revealing that the central essence of all true prophecy is bearing witness to Jesus. Revelation 19:10 (KJV) - "And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy."

question: How does John describe the glorious Warrior riding upon a white horse when heaven opened in Revelation 19:11-13?
opt1: He that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God
opt2: He was called the Prince of Peace, riding without weapons, clothed in a seamless Galilean tunic
opt3: He was called the High Priest of Israel, riding a white mule, wearing the golden breastplate of Aaron
opt4: He was called the Emperor of Rome, wearing an imperial laurel wreath, holding a scroll of civil laws
correct: He that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God
explanation: Jesus Christ descends as divine Conqueror and righteous Judge: Faithful and True, with eyes of fire, many royal diadems, a blood-dipped robe, and His eternal title 'The Word of God'. Revelation 19:11-13 (KJV) - "And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God."

question: Who followed the Rider on the white horse out of heaven, and how were they mounted and clothed?
opt1: The kings of the Gentiles followed Him upon black horses, armed with iron swords and bronze shields
opt2: And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean
opt3: The seventy elders of Israel followed Him upon golden chariots, blowing silver trumpets of war
opt4: The four living creatures followed Him on flying eagles, carrying bowls of burning coals
correct: And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean
explanation: The celestial armies of saints and angels accompany Christ on white mounts, robed in immaculate, pure white linen without earthly weaponry. Revelation 19:14 (KJV) - "And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean."

question: What instrument of judgment proceeds out of His mouth, and what supreme title is inscribed upon His vesture and thigh?
opt1: Out of His mouth goeth a golden scepter to bless the rulers... and on His vesture is written, PROPHET OF PROPHETS
opt2: Out of His mouth goeth a stream of pure water to quench the nations... and on His vesture is written, PRIEST OF PRIESTS
opt3: Out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron... and he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS
opt4: Out of His mouth goeth a blast of many trumpets to alarm the earth... and on His vesture is written, JUDGE OF JUDGES
correct: Out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron... and he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS
explanation: With the piercing sword of His spoken Word He smites the rebellious nations, bearing the sovereign banner of absolute universal supremacy: 'KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.' Revelation 19:15-16 (KJV) - "And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God. And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS."

question: What invitation did an angel standing in the sun proclaim unto all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven?
opt1: Fly unto the mountains of Media and build your nests, for the earth shall be covered with floodwaters
opt2: Descend upon the golden altars of the temple and eat of the grain offerings of the twenty-four elders
opt3: Flee from the face of the Rider on the white horse, for the fire of heaven shall consume the atmosphere
opt4: Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God; that ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men
correct: Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God; that ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men
explanation: An angel summons the birds of prey to feast upon the slaughtered armies of the Beast, known as the gruesome 'supper of the great God'. Revelation 19:17-18 (KJV) - "And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven, Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God; That ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses, and of them that sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great."

question: What immediate, horrific fate overtook the Beast and the False Prophet at the Battle of Armageddon?
opt1: These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone
opt2: They were imprisoned in subterranean iron cages beneath the ruins of the city of Rome
opt3: They were decapitated before the assembly of the saints, and their bodies cast into the Euphrates
opt4: They were banished into the desolate wastes of the Arabian desert for a thousand years
correct: These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone
explanation: Without prolonged battle, the Beast and his miracle-working False Prophet are captured and thrown alive into the Lake of Fire, becoming its first occupants. Revelation 19:20 (KJV) - "And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone."

question: How were the rest of the rebellious armies slain, and what gorged upon their remains?
opt1: They were drowned in a sudden deluge of oceanic waters, and the marine creatures consumed their bodies
opt2: And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh
opt3: They were struck down by an epidemic of pestilence, and buried in mass graves outside Jerusalem
opt4: They were swallowed alive into a fissure of the earth, and perished in the dark caves of Megiddo
correct: And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh
explanation: The assembled armies of the earth are slain by the word of Christ's mouth, and the scavenging birds are satiated with their flesh. Revelation 19:21 (KJV) - "And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh."

question: What did an angel descending from heaven do with the dragon, that old serpent called the Devil and Satan, in Revelation 20:1-3?
opt1: Executed the dragon upon the altar of heaven, and dissolved his spirit in the crystal sea forever
opt2: Chained the dragon to the seven hills of Rome, that the saints might mock his fallen majesty
opt3: Laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, and cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more
opt4: Transformed the dragon into a mortal man, that he might wander as a beggar throughout the nations
correct: Laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, and cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more
explanation: Satan is seized by an angel holding a great chain and locked securely in the abyss for 1,000 years to prevent him from deceiving the nations during the Millennium. Revelation 20:1-3 (KJV) - "And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season."

question: Who sat upon thrones to reign with Christ during the thousand years, and what is this resurrection called?
opt1: The kings of the Gentiles who established peaceful laws on earth; this is the second resurrection
opt2: The angels who guarded the churches of Asia Minor; this is the angelic resurrection
opt3: The ancient patriarchs from Adam to Noah alone; this is the patriarchal resurrection
opt4: The souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark... and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. This is the first resurrection
correct: The souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark... and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. This is the first resurrection
explanation: Resurrected martyrs and faithful saints reign with Christ for 1,000 years; this bodily resurrection of the righteous unto life is designated 'the first resurrection'. Revelation 20:4-5 (KJV) - "And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection."

question: What beatitude and priestly promise are pronounced upon those who share in the first resurrection in Revelation 20:6?
opt1: Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years
opt2: Blessed are they that accumulate wealth, for they shall purchase the lands of Galilee and Phoenicia
opt3: Blessed are they that build stone sanctuaries, for their names shall be carved in Roman forums
opt4: Blessed are they that possess physical longevity, for they shall never experience old age on earth
correct: Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years
explanation: Participants in the first resurrection are holy and blessed, completely immune to the second death (the lake of fire), serving as priests and co-rulers with Christ throughout the millennium. Revelation 20:6 (KJV) - "Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years."

question: When the thousand years are expired, what does Satan do upon being released from prison?
opt1: Shall repent before the throne of God in sackcloth and ashes, begging for eternal pardon
opt2: Shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea
opt3: Shall hide in subterranean caverns beneath the ocean, fleeing from the face of the saints
opt4: Shall challenge Michael the archangel to single combat outside the gates of Jerusalem
correct: Shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea
explanation: Released briefly, Satan immediately mobilizes a vast, final global rebellion from unregenerate humanity (Gog and Magog), numbering like the sand of the seashore. Revelation 20:7-8 (KJV) - "And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea."

question: What city and encampment did the armies of Gog and Magog surround, and how was their rebellion instantly crushed?
opt1: They surrounded the city of Rome, and an earthquake swallowed forty thousand soldiers into the abyss
opt2: They marched against the island of Patmos, and a tidal wave drowned their cavalry in the sea
opt3: They compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them
opt4: They besieged the mountain of Sinai, and dense darkness struck all their warriors with sudden blindness
correct: They compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them
explanation: As they encircle the saints and Jerusalem ('the beloved city'), supernatural fire descends directly from God out of heaven, utterly consuming the rebellious horde. Revelation 20:9 (KJV) - "And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them."

question: What final, eternal retribution did the devil receive following his defeated rebellion in Revelation 20:10?
opt1: The devil was bound in the bottomless pit for an additional seven thousand years of darkness
opt2: The devil was dissolved into cosmic nothingness, ceasing to exist as a conscious entity
opt3: The devil was banished into the outer regions of planetary space away from all creation
opt4: The devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever
correct: The devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever
explanation: Satan is consigned to the Lake of Fire to join the Beast and False Prophet in unending, conscious torment day and night for all eternity. Revelation 20:10 (KJV) - "And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever."

question: How does John describe the Great White Throne and the cosmic reaction of creation before Him who sat upon it?
opt1: I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them
opt2: I saw an altar of brass, and before it the twenty-four elders offered morning sacrifices for the dead
opt3: I saw a golden judgment seat erected in Jerusalem, and Caesar stood to plead his cause before Christ
opt4: I saw an emerald canopy resting upon Mount Zion, and the rivers of the earth flowed with sweet wine
correct: I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them
explanation: The final judicial scene features a majestic white throne whose blazing holiness causes the physical heavens and earth to dissolve and flee away. Revelation 20:11 (KJV) - "And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them."

question: Who stood before the Great White Throne, and on what basis were the dead judged in Revelation 20:12?
opt1: I saw only the rulers and kings of the earth stand, and they were judged according to their military prowess
opt2: I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works
opt3: I saw only the pagan philosophers stand, and they were judged according to their intellectual discourses
opt4: I saw only the false prophets stand, and they were judged according to their deceptive incantations
correct: I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works
explanation: All the unsaved dead of all generations stand before God; accurate records of their deeds in 'the books' provide the indisputable evidence for their individualized judgment. Revelation 20:12 (KJV) - "And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works."

question: What sources delivered up their dead to face this final judgment before being cast into the lake of fire?
opt1: The cities of Rome and Alexandria gave up their dead, and cast their idols into the sea
opt2: The rivers of the Euphrates and Nile delivered up their dead, and dissolved into salt
opt3: The sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them... And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death
opt4: The mountain caves of Patmos delivered up their dead, and crumbled into fine dust
correct: The sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them... And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death
explanation: Every physical and intermediate spiritual repository surrenders its dead, culminating in Death and Hades themselves being permanently abolished in the Lake of Fire (the second death). Revelation 20:13-14 (KJV) - "And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death."

question: What is the decisive, eternal criterion for escaping the lake of fire in the final judgment?
opt1: Whosoever failed to memorize the genealogy of the twelve tribes of Israel
opt2: Whosoever did not possess Roman citizenship or municipal certificates of good conduct
opt3: Whosoever failed to offer monetary tithes at the temple treasury in Jerusalem
opt4: And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire
correct: And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire
explanation: Absence from the sovereign Book of Life results in the inescapable, irrevocable consignment of the unredeemed to the Lake of Fire. Revelation 20:15 (KJV) - "And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire."

question: What new cosmic order did John behold when the first heaven and first earth passed away in Revelation 21:1?
opt1: A new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea
opt2: A restored earthly kingdom of Judea: and the Mediterranean sea was doubled in commercial depth
opt3: A celestial sphere of perpetual ice: and the sun was extinguished from shining forever
opt4: A spiritual void of silence: and physical creation was permanently erased from memory
correct: A new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea
explanation: Following the dissolution of the corrupted cosmos, God creates a pristine New Heaven and New Earth, where chaotic, separating oceans exist no more. Revelation 21:1 (KJV) - "And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea."

question: How does John describe the descent of the New Jerusalem from heaven in Revelation 21:2?
opt1: The imperial city of Rome, built with marble and gold by the architects of Caesar
opt2: The holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband
opt3: The ancient fortress of Zion, repaired with cedar beams and iron gates by the patriarchs
opt4: The temple of Alexandria, floating upon clouds and surrounded by seven archangels
correct: The holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband
explanation: The New Jerusalem descends directly from God, personified and prepared in dazzling bridal beauty for eternal union with Christ. Revelation 21:2 (KJV) - "And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband."

question: What grand proclamation of divine dwelling and comfort did John hear from heaven in Revelation 21:3-4?
opt1: Behold, the laws of Moses are enforced across all planets, and angels shall rule over mortal cities
opt2: Behold, the wealth of Egypt is distributed unto all nations, and physical poverty is ended on earth
opt3: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain
opt4: Behold, the gates of the temple are opened for annual sacrifices, and the priests shall burn incense
correct: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain
explanation: The ultimate goal of redemption is realized: unhindered fellowship with God, who wipes away every tear and abolishes death, sorrow, crying, and pain forever. Revelation 21:3-4 (KJV) - "And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away."

question: What absolute assurance of renewal and free spiritual drink does He that sat upon the throne proclaim in Revelation 21:5-6?
opt1: Behold, I restore the ancient laws of Aaron... Buy of Me gold and silver to purchase an entrance into the city
opt2: Behold, I rebuild the towers of David... Offer daily animal sacrifices to maintain peace in the sanctuary
opt3: Behold, I establish Roman citizenship in heaven... Obey the decrees of the twenty-four elders
opt4: Behold, I make all things new... It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely
correct: Behold, I make all things new... It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely
explanation: God Himself guarantees universal renewal ('all things new') and invites every thirsty soul to drink without cost from the life-giving fountain of grace. Revelation 21:5-6 (KJV) - "And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful. And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely."

question: What heritage belongs to the overcomer, and who are excluded and consigned to the lake of fire in Revelation 21:7-8?

opt4: The overcomer shall govern the Roman senate; but those who refused circumcision shall be imprisoned

But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone
explanation: Overcomers inherit full filial sonship and all things, while the unrepentant wicked (cowardly, unbelieving, sexually immoral, occultists, idolaters, liars) share the second death. Revelation 21:7-8 (KJV) - "He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son. But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death."

question: How does John describe the wall, gates, and foundations of the holy city New Jerusalem in Revelation 21:12-14?
opt1: Had seven gates with seven archangels inscribed with the planets, and four foundations named after the evangelists
opt2: Had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel... And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb
opt3: Had twenty-four iron towers guarded by centurions, and twelve foundations inscribed with the kings of Judah
opt4: Had three marble gates named after the patriarchs, and forty foundations inscribed with the prophets

explanation: The New Jerusalem unites all the redeemed: its twelve gates bear the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and its twelve foundation stones bear the names of the Lamb's twelve apostles. Revelation 21:12-14 (KJV) - "And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: On the east three gates; on the north three gates; on the south three gates; and on the west three gates. And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb."

question: What geometric shape and staggering dimensions characterized the holy city measured by the angel with a golden reed?
opt1: The city was a great circle, seventy furlongs in circumference, surrounded by an iron moat of water
opt2: The city was a massive pyramid, three hundred cubits high, constructed of polished marble blocks
opt3: The city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal
opt4: The city was an octagon, forty furlongs wide, flanked by twenty-four golden towers of refuge
correct: The city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal
explanation: The city is a perfect cube (12,000 stadia / approx. 1,400-1,500 miles on each side), echoing the cubic dimensions of the Holy of Holies where God's presence dwells. Revelation 21:16 (KJV) - "And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal."

question: What precious materials composed the twelve gates and the street of the New Jerusalem in Revelation 21:21?

opt3: And the twelve gates were twelve monoliths of cedar: every several gate was of scented wood: and the street of the city was alabaster marble
opt4: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls: every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass

explanation: The holy city radiates unearthly perfection: each immense portal is fashioned from a single magnificent pearl, opening onto a main street of transparent gold. Revelation 21:21 (KJV) - "And the twelve gates were twelve pearls: every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass."

question: Why was there no physical temple in the New Jerusalem, and what provided its perpetual illumination?
opt1: And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof

explanation: No separate temple is needed because the immediate presence of the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb permeates all space, His uncreated glory providing eternal light. Revelation 21:22-23 (KJV) - "And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof."

question: What absolute exclusion guarantees the eternal purity of the New Jerusalem in Revelation 21:27?
opt1: No man without Roman citizenship or municipal letters of commendation may enter through the gates

explanation: Total sanctity is preserved: anything defiling, abominable, or deceitful is permanently excluded; entrance is granted solely to those recorded in the Lamb's Book of Life. Revelation 21:27 (KJV) - "And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb's book of life."

question: What river did the angel show John in the holy city, and from where does it proceed?
opt1: A river of melted silver, proceeding out of the golden altar of incense in the temple

opt4: A river of boiling oil, proceeding out of the bottomless pit to consume the works of the wicked
correct: A pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb
explanation: The River of Life flows crystal clear through the city, proceeding directly from the joint throne of God and the Lamb, symbolizing eternal, revitalizing fellowship. Revelation 22:1 (KJV) - "And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb."

question: What tree stood on either side of the river, and what dual blessings do its fruit and leaves provide?

opt3: The vine of Eschol, which yielded clusters of purple grapes every season to brew wine for angels
opt4: The tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations

explanation: The Tree of Life flourishes on both river banks, yielding perpetual monthly harvests of life-giving fruit, with leaves promoting the eternal well-being of the redeemed nations. Revelation 22:2 (KJV) - "In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations."

question: What glorious conditions characterize the eternal state in Revelation 22:3-5 regarding the curse, service, and vision of God?
opt1: And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: and they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads

opt3: The saints shall wander as invisible spirits throughout the universe, forgetting their earthly pilgrimage

explanation: The Edenic curse is totally abolished; believers engage in joyous active service, behold God's face in intimate communion (the beatific vision), and reign forever in His light. Revelation 22:3-5 (KJV) - "And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads. And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever."

question: What beatitude does Jesus pronounce in Revelation 22:7 regarding His imminent coming and prophetic obedience?

opt4: Behold, I come to restore the temple of Solomon: blessed is he that builds an altar of marble
correct: Behold, I come quickly: blessed is he that keepeth the sayings of the prophecy of this book
explanation: Christ announces His sudden, imminent return, pronouncing a special blessing upon everyone who treasures and obeys the prophetic words of this book. Revelation 22:7 (KJV) - "Behold, I come quickly: blessed is he that keepeth the sayings of the prophecy of this book."

question: Why was John commanded not to seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, unlike Daniel of old?
opt1: Seal up the prophecy in a bronze cylinder, for many centuries of darkness must pass first

correct: Seal not the sayings of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand
explanation: Unlike Daniel (told to seal his book until the time of the end), John is commanded to leave Revelation open and accessible because the era of fulfillment is immediately present. Revelation 22:10 (KJV) - "And he saith unto me, Seal not the sayings of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand."

question: What sovereign declaration and titles does Jesus Christ announce in Revelation 22:12-13?
opt1: I come with the legions of Caesar; and My tribute is with Me, to reward all municipal tax collectors

opt3: I come as a philosophical master; and My books are with Me, to instruct the scholars of Alexandria

explanation: Christ proclaims His return as righteous rewarder, reaffirming His eternal divinity through the threefold title: Alpha and Omega, Beginning and End, First and Last. Revelation 22:12-13 (KJV) - "And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last."

question: What beatitude is pronounced upon those who do His commandments, and who are permanently left outside the holy city?

explanation: Obedient believers receive the right of access to the Tree of Life and entry through the gates, while unrepentant sinners of every stripe are excluded forever. opt4: I Jesus have sent Michael to overthrow the pagan monuments and statues of Caesar

explanation: Jesus authenticates the entire book as His personal communication to the churches, identifying Himself as David's divine Creator and human Descendant, and the radiant Morning Star. Revelation 22:16 (KJV) - "I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star."

question: What universal, gracious gospel invitation is extended in Revelation 22:17?

Revelation 22:17 (KJV) - "And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely."

question: What solemn warning seals the integrity of the prophetic words of this book against adding or taking away in Revelation 22:18-19?

explanation: Holy Scripture closes with a fearsome prohibition against altering God's Word under penalty of divine plagues and forfeiture of eternal life in the holy city. Revelation 22:18-19 (KJV) - "For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book."
